ahead: s8_control.py's scan for exceptional data uses C0=0.05 as a stand-in for TT Definition 2.1's 'sufficiently small absolute constant' c_0, which is not pinned to a number anywhere in SIEGEL_UNIFORMITY.md or CORRECTED_RH_BRIDGE.md; the scan pads 0.3 below the resulting window before searching, so a smaller true c_0 (which only shrinks the window toward s=1) cannot flip a 'no_exception' verdict here into a missed zero, but a future attempt tightening this should know the constant is chosen, not derived. Also: for all five required cutoffs Z(N)=exp((log N)^0.1) stays below 3.6 (it does not reach 4 until N~10^12), so q=3 is the only candidate conductor ever checked in this run; correction_vector()'s general C_N(h) branch (used only if an exceptional zero is ever found) calls mp.quad once per shift h and was not exercised at the scale of N=100000, so its performance at large N with an actual exceptional case is unverified. All required rows came back 'no_exception', so E_corr(N)==E(N) exactly at every N in {2000,5000,10000,30000,100000}; the sensitivity table in S8_CONTROL.md section 3 is the only place E_corr and E diverge in this deliverable.
